title: Senior Software Engineer - Husky Storage
locationText: Boston, Massachusetts, USA; New York, New York, USA
description:
Husky is what we call the distributed, petabyte-scale columnar event store at the heart of our Event Platform, which powers dozens of Datadog’s most popular products - Logs, RUM, APM, Cloud Network Monitoring, Netflow, and many more. Husky was built from the ground up at Datadog to store and query massive volumes of event data at low cost, with data fully queryable within seconds of arrival.

 

As a Senior Software Engineer on this team, you'll work hands-on with a distributed storage system at petabyte scale, and help us evolve our platform to support the next level of scale that will power the AI era. We will move from a custom storage format towards open standards (Parquet, Arrow, DataFusion) enabling on prem solutions, increasingly complex analytical/batch workloads, and powering AI observability, sustainably into the future. You'll partner closely with Husky Ingestion, Metadata, and Platform, and increasingly with Lakehouse on the Iceberg-compatible boundary between Husky and analytical/batch workloads. You will also work with the open source community to  build the next generation of reusable software solutions that can be operated at scale.

 

Datadog has a culture that is increasingly rare in mature technology companies. We are an engineering driven, bottom up, high agency/high responsibility culture-where everyone is empowered and expected to drive the technological and strategic direction of the business over time. We are a blameless culture where we believe supporting each other through challenges produces the best outcomes over time and our track record corroborates this. We are open source champions. We believe in the flexibility of working remotely but also the value of bringing people together across our various offices worldwide-and our offices are nice places to work.

What You’ll Do: 

• Drive Husky to the next level of adoption by migrating our storage format to open source Parquet and re-imagine compaction on a format-agnostic, DataFusion-based substrate

• Drive concrete cost-reduction work: block-level inverted index compression, combining the database with external objects at the row level, and storage tiering/caching

• Scale our solution to enable customers to manage event versioning at scale, using temporal-database techniques.

• Play an influential role in operating and deciding how to best operate our service going forward.

• Work across the write path (with Ingestion) and toward a cleaner Iceberg-based handoff to ADP/Lakehouse for batch/analytical workloads

Who You Are: 

• Enthusiastic and experienced with large-scale distributed systems and/or storage engines

• Comfortable with improving and operating large distributed systems that customers rely on for critical business functions

• Strong fundamentals in columnar/file storage formats (Parquet, ORC, Arrow) or comparable systems

• Bonus : experience with Go, Java, or Rust; with compaction or compression/encoding schemes (RLE, dictionary, delta, gorilla); with object storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) at scale, including caching and cost optimization; with Kafka and stream processing; or with Kubernetes

 

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply. 

 

Benefits and Growth: 

• New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan (ESPP)

• Continuous professional development, product training, and career pathing

• Intradepartmental mentor and buddy program for in-house networking

• An inclusive company culture, ability to join our Community Guilds (Datadog employee resource groups)

• Free, global mental health benefits for employees and dependents age 6+

Benefits and Growth listed above may vary based on the country of your employment and the nature of your employment with Datadog.

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
About Us

We are customer-obsessed to an unusual degree. When we had a major network outage, everyone, including recruiters, engineers, and marketers, got on the phone with customers. That’s not a policy. It’s just who we are.

What keeps us going is what we hear from our Community. Families tell us they used to wake up every morning with a knot in their stomach. They don’t anymore. They tell us our product changed their relationship with their parents, from anxious and fearful to present and connected. It’s genuinely important work, and we don’t take it lightly.

If that’s the kind of problem you want to spend the next few years on, one with real scale, real mission, real momentum, and a real Community of people behind it, we’d love to talk.

Why this role exists

Communications for the aging in America are broken. Seniors are isolated. Their families are anxious in ways that go far beyond "I hope mom's alright." James Graham started this company after seeing his own grandmother get taken advantage of by the large telecom hegemony.

They are checking her bank account daily because they cannot tell if she is being scammed. They are calling three times a day because she did not pick up and they do not know if she is okay. They are lying awake wondering if she is connected to anyone, or just sitting alone. And at the most basic level, a lot of their phone service is completely unreliable or breaks entirely for the family once she reaches a certain age.

There are 55 million Americans over 65 living at home. Most of them, and most of their families, are navigating this alone.

Community Phone solves that. We built a phone so simple it works out of the box, no setup required. We wrapped it with AI-powered check-in calls that surface how she is really doing. And we built a family app integrated to Mom’s phone that replaces daily dread with genuine safety and peace of mind.

It is working. We are well into 8-figure subscription ARR, pacing to 9-figure, with 30,000+ families trusting us with something that matters deeply to them. Customers stay. They refer their friends. They tell us we took away an anxiety they had carried for years.

We are a lean, product-driven team. The people who thrive here take full ownership, are mission-driven, move quickly, hyper-curious, and care deeply about the customer. One of our product engineers won an Oscar for best foreign film, one team member is a Thiel Fellow, one is a Harvard Philosophy PhD dropout, others are the first growth hires at now-unicorn companies, others of our product engineers are former leaders of 60+ person engineering organizations, and many are former founders.

What you'll own

•
Set design strategy across the full customer journey - physical unboxing, mobile app, web dashboard, agentic ai voice check ins, etc - treating them as one coherent customer story end to end with clearly divided responsibilities, not surfaces competing for the same features or moments of customer attention throughout time.

•
Own outcomes past first activation. At this scale, getting someone through setup is only half the job - you'll be on the team accountable for adoption impact (AI check-in calls, call forwarding, spam blocking, call monitoring & safety features) and the metrics that show whether customers actually get value, in partnership with growth and PLG-focused teams. You are constantly learning post launch about how launched design can be improved.

•
Mock up full working prototypes: You should be completely fluent with modern AI development tools and be able to show full working mockups quickly. To the team. To customers in the ICP. To the CEO. You are AI optimistic and not AI psychotic.

•
Build the foundations a growing design org will need : a shared component language across app, dashboard, AI & sound interface, a research and testing habit (especially with lower-tech-literacy and senior users), and documentation that lets non-designers make good small decisions without you in the roo

• Driving unit economics analysis across clients and revenue streams

• Leading cash flow management and financial planning in a high-growth environment

• Ensuring tax, regulatory, and compliance alignment with our Cyprus-based legal entity

• Acting as a strategic partner to leadership on growth decisions and capital allocation

• 5-7 years of experience in finance, accounting, FP&A, or corporate finance

• Strong bookkeeping and accounting fundamentals

• Excellent financial modelling and analytical skills

• Exposure to tech, digital advertising, SaaS, or high-growth startups

• Understanding of revenue models, margins, and unit economics

• ACCA/ACA qualified (or equivalent)

• Knowledge on VAT & VIES reporting in the EU

• EU market experience, ideally with multiple companies

• The ability to operate in a fast-moving, sometimes ambiguous environment

• A mindset that combines ownership, precision, and strategic thinking

• Experience with scaling finance functions is a strong advantage.

• Advance experience working with Xero (software).

Why This Role Works Remotely
We operate as a remote-first team, working with talent across multiple countries while our legal entity and corporate structure are based in Cyprus.
This allows you to:

• Work fully remotely while contributing to a global business

• Operate within a stable EU framework

• Collaborate with an international team in a fast-moving industry

We care far more about capability, ownership, and impact than where you sit.
Why This Role Is Different
Many finance roles support growth.
This one helps design it.
You wont just inherit systems-youll build them.
You wont just report numbers-youll own them end-to-end.
For the right candidate, this is a chance to grow into the role of CFO while helping build a company at the same time.
Interested?
If this sounds like the kind of opportunity where you could do your best work, apply now.
Were excited to meet finance leaders who are ready to step up, take ownership, and grow with us.

This hire will be instrumental in signaling and forecasting accurate demand, planning inventory levels, and ensuring that Anduril supports its hardware requirements via Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) software and other associated tools.

The right person for this role has demonstrate ownership and experience solving complex operational challenges with creative solutions in a fast-paced, resource-limited environment. This person will be flexible to provide support wherever needed to ensure products are built and shipped under stringent quality standards. If you are someone who thrives in such an environment, then this role is for you!

• Identify and resolve supply issues by collaborating with Engineering, Purchasing, and Manufacturing teams.

title: Data API Engineer
description:
ABOUT SUPABASE

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Data API Engineer to join our Data API Team and help improve the feature set, reliability and performance of our Data API, based on the PostgREST project.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

- Work on PostgREST’s PostgreSQL driver (based on Hasql) and remove bottlenecks and improve it’s performance.

- Work on PostgREST development of new features and bug fixes, aligned towards the goal of a multitenant Data API.

- Resolve incidents and escalated support issues, while also improving observability and performance.

- Collaborate cross-functionally with other teams to debug and solve integration issues with the Supabase platform.

YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

- Strong Haskell skills with at least 3 years of experience.

- Experience using the C language.

- Solid knowledge of SQL and plpgsql scripting in PostgreSQL.

- Strong track record of contributing to and engaging with open-source projects. Bonus points if you’ve maintained an open source project.

- Strong experience with providing technical support to users with varying levels of technical expertise.

- Experience with debugging applications under the Linux operating system.

WHAT WE OFFER

- Fully Remote

We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

- ESOP

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

- Tech Allowance

Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment-laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

- Health Benefits

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

- Annual Off-Sites

Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

- Flexible Work

We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

- Professional Development

Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning-courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

- ~400 team members

- 60+ countries

- 20+ languages spoken

- Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

- 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support-not replace-existing tools and communities.

title: Senior Product Manager, Access Management
description:
Who We Are

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management. 

We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation , more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it.

You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries. 

The Opportunity

Every day, a security administrator somewhere decides who can open which door. A new nurse starts on Monday and needs the medication room but not the server closet. A contractor needs the loading dock for three weeks. Someone leaves the company at 5pm and their badge should stop working at 5:01. Multiply that by 200,000 employees across 400 sites, and you have one of the largest and least-solved logistical problems in enterprise software.

Access control is Verkada's second largest business: hundreds of millions of dollars in sales, growing 40 to 60% year over year, with roughly 80 people building in this area. Access management is the pillar that decides whether all of that feels effortless or exhausting.

We are hiring a Lead Product Manager to own it end to end: users, identities, groups, policies, requests, access levels, and visitor access, from the moment an admin expresses intent to the moment a door opens for the right person.

We do this well today. We think it can be dramatically better, through interfaces that make scale feel simple, APIs and integrations that let the system run itself, and agents that let an admin state what they want instead of clicking through configuration. You will own that as a vertical slice: web and mobile, the backend behind them, the configuration we push to door hardware, and the API and agent surfaces we expose. You will work with a dedicated designer, an engineering manager, and a dedicated engineering team.

We are committed to a thriving in-office culture. This role requires you to work onsite at our HQ in San Mateo, CA.

The access model and administrator interfaces: get the core concepts right

• Own users, groups, credentials, access levels, door associations, and schedules. This is the conceptual core of the product, and getting it right is the difference between an admin who trusts the system and one who works around it

• Own the administrative interfaces and experience across web and mobile: bulk operations, search, and review flows that stay fast when a customer has 200,000 users and 10,000 doors

• Own visitor access, including how guests are invited, credentialed, and expired

Provisioning and integrations: let the system run itself

• Own the API and integration surface. Most large customers want access to follow their identity provider and HR system automatically, so joiners, movers, and leavers are handled without anyone touching our UI

• Partner with Verkada's Core team to drive identity integration: SCIM provisioning, SSO, directory sync, and the mapping between an HR record and what a door actually does

Agents and natural language: let admins state intent

• Define how agents fit into access management. An admin should be able to say what they want and have the system propose the configuration that satisfies it

title: Sr. Staff Product Manager, AI-Native IT Service Management
description:
About the team
Service Operations is where enterprises find out whether their technology actually works. An outage starts, someone gets paged, a bridge call spins up, and the first twenty minutes go to working out what broke rather than fixing it.
Our team owns the products that close that gap: incident and major incident, problem and root cause, change, on-call, and Notify. The people using them go well beyond the service desk, from application, platform, infrastructure, and network teams to DevOps and SRE groups who get alerted around the clock and the major incident commanders pulling everyone onto one call. Thousands of the largest IT organizations run their operations on these products. We are rebuilding them AI-native, not AI-assisted, with agents that triage, correlate, and resolve, and with people moving from doing the work to directing it. Our goal is Zero Service Outage.
About the role
You will own a piece of that portfolio outright: what good looks like for it, who it is for, and whether we are honestly there yet. Zero Service Outage is the goal, and the work is making it true for the customers who run their operations on these products every day.
The interesting part of this job is not the model. It is the environment it runs in. Service operations data is the messiest data in the enterprise: half-populated CMDBs, incident descriptions written in a hurry at 2am, alert noise from a dozen monitoring tools, and naming conventions that differ by region. An agent that triages perfectly against a clean eval set can behave very differently against a real customer’s incident stream, for reasons that have nothing to do with reasoning ability. Understanding why, and designing for it, is the job.
We also carry an installed base. Customers run today’s experience in production, and moving them onto an AI-native one is not a UI refresh. It is a change to how their IT team works, who approves what, and what an operator trusts an agent to do unsupervised. You will be making calls about what we carry forward, what we leave behind, and what we have to earn the right to automate.
How we work is changing as fast as what we build. Prototype instead of describing the idea. Put a working demo in front of people instead of a slide about a demo. Draft the spec, stand up a rough eval harness, pull your own data. ServiceNow invests in state-of-the-art tooling and expects you to use it. Product managers are better positioned than anyone to lead that shift, and part of this role is pulling the team around you into it.
What you get to do in this role

• Own an AI-native ITSM product end to end, from the customer problem through launch criteria to how it performs in production.

• Set product strategy for the Service Operations portfolio that supports ServiceNow ’s growth toward $10B+ in revenue.

• Build, not just specify. Prototype the interaction, stand up the eval harness, and get into the agent execution logs to understand what happened on the runs that failed.

• Define what good means for an autonomous agent in an operational context where the cost of a wrong action is a second outage. Hold the line on it with engineering and have the honest conversation about what we can defensibly promise.

• Work with design partners across the teams that run on this: service desk, application and infrastructure support, DevOps and SRE, and major incident command. Build in their environment against their real incidents, changes, and RCAs, then turn what you learn into something that generalizes to the next thousand customers.

• Own your outcome metrics, such as time to resolve, change failure rate, and repeat incidents, in partnership with Customer Success, and make sure the instrumentation exists to show whether what you shipped moved them.

• Align with peer product managers so the team is working on the right things at the right time and guide multiple teams through ambiguous product development without losing sight of the unified vision.

• Write

title: Senior Product Manager
description:
About Learning Sandbox

We create learning experiences that engage, empower and inspire. Learning Sandbox is a global learning consultancy bringing together learning, creativity and technology to help organisations solve meaningful learning challenges.
Our work spans digital learning, education, science, technology and everything in between. We work with ambitious organisations and multidisciplinary teams to turn complex ideas into experiences that are clear, engaging and impactful.
We’re a curious, collaborative team that cares about putting people first, growing together and doing exceptional work that enriches the world.
About our client: LabXchange
LabXchange is a nonprofit education project based at Harvard University. Too many students, whether because of economic or geographic limitations, lack access to high-quality science education and the chance to engage meaningfully in the scientific process. Globally, this has led to significant gaps in diversity across scientific fields and in scientific literacy overall. LabXchange believes students everywhere should have an equal opportunity to prepare for and succeed in science.
To make that real, LabXchange offers the best of digital science education to teachers and students around the world, for free, through an advanced, flexible and interactive learning platform. It goes well beyond text, video and multiple-choice questions, with virtual lab simulations, interactive animations, experimental design simulations and a knowledge graph that can be remixed into customised learning pathways. Social features like private classes, discussion forums and mentorship connect learners with educators.
About the role
We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to own growth for the LabXchange platform: more learners and educators finding it, and more of them coming back. You'll set the growth strategy, turn data into a clear roadmap, and work with engineering, design, content and marketing to ship experiments that move acquisition, activation and engagement. This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who is as comfortable in a dashboard as in a roadmap review.
What you’ll be doing

• Own the growth strategy for LabXchange across acquisition, activation, engagement and retention, and turn it into a prioritised roadmap. This will include the USA and a global strategy.

• Grow the user base by finding and scaling the channels that bring in students, educators and institutions, including organic search, marketing, partnerships and referral loops.

• Increase engagement by improving onboarding, discovery and the paths that bring learners and educators back week after week.

• Lead with data. Define the growth metrics, build and maintain dashboards, run funnel and cohort analysis, and use the findings to decide what to build next.

• Run a steady experimentation programme: form hypotheses, design A/B tests, size impact and share what you learn.

• Drive SEO and content discoverability with content and engineering teams, so our simulations, lessons and pathways reach people searching for them.

• Manage the core library experience: how learners and educators find, browse and reach the right content, and how the library is organised so that it happens quickly. Manage the development and redesign of the LabXchange platform.

• Work across teams with engineering, design, content, marketing and partners, and keep stakeholders and funders informed on progress and results.

• Manage stakeholders and projects across multiple capabilities (engineering, design, content, marketing and partners), keeping priorities, timelines, dependencies and expectations aligned from kickoff through delivery.

• Keep stakeholders in the loop. Announce releases in various Slack channels and facilitate catchups with various stakeholders.

• Bring in the user's voice through interviews, surveys and usability testing with students and educators around the world.

• Manage a multi-timezone team to achieve LabXchange’s growth goa

description:

title: Growth Marketing Manager, Events
description:
PermitFlow is redefining how America builds. We’re an applied AI company serving the nation’s builders, tackling one of the largest information challenges in the economy: understanding what can be built, where, and how . Our AI agent workforce helps the fastest-growing construction companies navigate everything from permitting and licensing to inspections and project closeouts - accelerating housing, clean-energy, and infrastructure development across the country.
Despite being a $1.6T industry, construction still suffers from massive delays, wasted capital, and lost opportunity. PermitFlow has already delivered unprecedented speed, accuracy, and visibility to over $20B in development, helping contractors reduce compliance time, de-risk projects, and scale with confidence.
As the U.S. enters a new capex supercycle across data centers, factories, housing, and renewables, joining PermitFlow means building the AI infrastructure at the core of every construction project driving the next wave of reindustrialization.
We’ve raised over $90M, most recently completing our Series B, from top-tier investors including Accel, Kleiner Perkins, Initialized, Y Combinator, Felicis, and Altos Ventures, with backing from leaders at OpenAI, Google, Procore, ServiceTitan, Zillow, PlanGrid, and Uber.
Our HQ is in New York City with a hybrid schedule (3 in-office days per week). We prefer NYC-based candidates or those open to relocation.
About the Role
We've built the foundation for events at PermitFlow . Now we need someone to own the outcome and turn events into a pillar of our GTM motion.
This role runs the full events portfolio: industry conferences, owned events, customer-specific gatherings, and field marketing, plus ongoing experimentation with new formats, venues, and audiences. You'll execute hands-on, with internal and external support, and tie every event back to pipeline and revenue goals. We're an experimentation-heavy culture. What You'll Do

• Own the events portfolio: build the calendar across industry events, owned events, customer events, and field marketing, and decide where to place bets.

• Run logistics end to end: venues, budgets, vendors, contractors, staffing, and the on-the-ground run of show.

• Experiment deliberately and iterate quickly: test new formats, venues, and target audiences, and kill what doesn't work.

• Get the right targets in the room and at our booth. Great events don't stop at a project plan; they rely on driving high-value attendees.

• Connect events to revenue: define what success looks like for each event, track pipeline and revenue impact, and report results back to the business.

• Partner cross-functionally: work closely with demand gen, product marketing, sales, CS, and business operations to align events with GTM priorities.

• Manage event budgets and vendor relationships: negotiate contracts, manage contractor relationships, and keep spend accountable.

• Build the playbook: turn what's worked into repeatable processes so the program scales as the business grows.

• Represent events at the leadership level: bring recommendations and results directly to company leadership.

• Source speaking opportunities at relevant industry and public events for executive leadership, including content submissions as needed.

Who You Are

• 4-7+ years running B2B events in a fast-moving environment and know the difference between an event that just looks good and one that drives pipeline.

• You can run logistics yourself. You don't need a coordinator to book a venue or manage a floor plan, but you know when and what to delegate.

• You think like a marketer first and an event planner second: every event ties back to organizational goals.

title: Associate Counsel
description:
More than 80% of Americans own a car and see it as a fundamental necessity, yet the experience of owning one is stuck in the 90s. At Jerry .ai, we are building the first app to manage it all. Since launching in 2019, we’ve reached 5M+ customers, raised $240M+, scaled revenue 70X, and achieved profitability in 2024.
Operating across the U.S. and Canada brings a steady flow of commercial, regulatory, consumer protection, and product questions. As our Associate Counsel, you’ll report directly to our Legal Counsel and work with teams across Jerry to turn complex legal issues into practical that help the business move forward.
This role is designed for a lawyer with law firm and/or in-house experience who wants broad responsibility in a growing technology company. You’ll draft and negotiate agreements, advise on product and compliance questions, and drive assigned matters from initial assessment through resolution. You’ll develop your own recommendations and manage day-to-day execution, bringing significant decisions and novel or higher-risk issues to our Legal Counsel.
Why You Will (Or Won’t) Like Working Here

• Substantive ownership: You’ll manage matters, work directly with business partners, and bring a clear point of view. You’ll need to distinguish the issues that matter from those that can be resolved pragmatically.

• Broad exposure: Your work will span contracts, product launches, insurance and consumer regulation, privacy, and disputes. You don’t need to arrive as an expert in every area, but you should enjoy learning unfamiliar subjects and applying sound judgment.

• A small team with a hands-on approach: Our legal team is two people today. You’ll work closely with our cofounder and executives on legal issues that shape business decisions, organize your own matters, follow through on implementation, and help with operational details when needed.

• Technology as part of the work: We use AI and automation to improve research, drafting, and legal processes. You’ll be expected to use these tools thoughtfully, verify their output, and take responsibility for the quality of your work.

• Growth that tracks results: You’ll work with teammates from companies like Nvidia, Amazon, McKinsey, Bain, and BCG. Promotion is based on performance alone, so strong work moves you forward fast.

What You’ll Own

• Commercial agreements: Draft, review, and negotiate agreements with carriers, business partners, and vendors. Identify material risks, propose practical terms, and manage negotiations and internal coordination through execution.

• Product and regulatory advice: Research federal and state insurance, consumer protection, privacy, and other requirements. Translate your analysis into clear recommendations on new products, customer flows, disclosures, consent, marketing, and operational processes.

• Consumer escalations and regulatory matters: Investigate complex complaints and regulatory inquiries, identify relevant facts and legal issues, and prepare proposed responses. Work with Legal and business teams to resolve matters and address recurring causes.

• Compliance and risk management: Help design policies, procedures, training, and controls. Review audit findings, identify issues requiring legal judgment, and work with operational owners to implement and track corrective actions.

• Licensing and corporate matters: Address substantive questions arising from entity maintenance, licensing, appointments, and business expansion. Work with colleagues handling recurring compliance operations and escalate material risks.

• Emerging issues and legal processes: Take on new legal questions as Jerry launches products and enters partnerships. Improve templates, guidance, and workflows so the team can deliver consistent advice efficiently.

Who You Are

• Practical and Thoughtful: You develop a recommendation, explain your reasoning clearly, and balance legal risk with business objectives.

• An Accountable Owner: You keep matters moving,

title: Senior Manager - Global Product Ops Excellence (All Genders)
description:
The role

From day one you’ll enable international coordination and implementation of strategic product priorities by creating, standardising and optimising processes across central and local physical product teams and other stakeholders. The role will require a mix of process improvement, change management, technical understanding, project management and stakeholder management skills. Not only will you be an ambassador of Product Operations Excellence, but also champion the value of process automation and optimization, to set a solid basis for growth.

Above all, we are looking for people who will make HelloFresh better. We believe there are many different ways of developing skills and we love diverse experiences! So even if you don’t “tick all the boxes” but think you’d thrive in this role, we would really like to learn more about you.

What you’ll do

• Shape the operating model: Diagnose end-to-end processes across central and local Product teams and adjacent functions (Procurement, FSQA, Production). 

• Design and scale standards: Own process frameworks, SOPs and rollout "golden standards" that teams across markets adopt. Challenge and iterate existing policies and guidelines when they no longer fit the business.

• Lead cross-market change: Drive organizational change across markets and functions, balancing central consistency with local needs. Build alignment with senior stakeholders, resolve conflicts, and ensure a constant flow of information.

• Lead programs and automation: Own complex automation and tooling initiatives from a commercial perspective. Sign off on tooling designs and business cases, guide Tech teams on scope, edge cases and interdependencies, and take part in Steering Committees. On top of that, identify where AI can reshape Product Operations processes, build the business cases and prototypes, and deploy the successful tools across markets and teams. 

• Lead under uncertainty: Scope and drive short- and long-term programs from broadly defined outcomes. Develop plan Bs and alternative solutions when priorities shift, and turn ambiguous problems into manageable, measurable workstreams.

What you’ll bring

• 5+ years minimum experience in Product Operations or Operational/Process Excellence; passion for food or experience within Food/FMCG industry or consultancy is a plus

• Recognized expertise in process excellence, change management and program delivery, with advanced knowledge of methodologies, current best practices and industry trends. You continuously challenge the status quo and bring new ideas to life.

• Highly numerate and commercially minded, able to build rigorous, objective business cases and to judge technical designs with confidence.

• A strong stakeholder leader who manages global and local stakeholders at all levels, aligns teams across markets, and communicates clearly to different audiences.

• Autonomous and outcome-driven: you manage scope and timelines independently, prioritize relentlessly, and are comfortable being challenged on the soundness of your work.

• Thrives in a fast-paced, demanding and data-driven environment. 

• Curious about AI and automation: you actively explore how AI can reshape processes, assess its impact rigorously, and lead teams to adopt it where it creates measurable value.

• Bachelor's or Master's degree from a top-tier university, preferably in business, management, operations or a related field. Six Sigma Belt or PMP certification is a big plus.

Elevate your lifestyle! Join one of Europe's fastest-growing tech powerhouses in a dynamic phase of expansion.

title: Hardware Engineer, Core Technology

description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About the Role

We're looking for a Hardware Engineer for Special Projects to serve as Core Tech's go-to technical problem solver. You will be deployed across the portfolio wherever the highest-priority gap is: diagnosing a hardware integration issue on one program, standing up a demo for a customer visit the next week, writing test automation to close a verification gap, building an internal dashboard to track production yield, or untangling a process bottleneck that's slowing down an entire team. The common thread is that every problem is different, the timeline is always tight, and the solution requires someone who can move fluidly between mechanical hardware, electronics, software, and systems-level thinking. If you've spent your career building breadth across engineering disciplines and you'd rather solve the hardest problem in the room than own a single subsystem, this is the role.

• Own and execute short-duration, high-impact technical projects across Core Tech, scoped anywhere from a few days to a few months, spanning hardware, software, test, manufacturing, and process domains.

• Diagnose and resolve cross-functional technical issues (integration failures, test escapes, supplier quality problems, production-line bottlenecks) by getting hands-on with the hardware, the data, or the code as needed.

• Plan and execute customer and internal demonstrations end-to-end: define the demo architecture, coordinate resources, prepare technical materials, verify system readiness, and run the demo.

• Develop test software, automation scripts, and data-analysis tools (Python, MATLAB, or similar) to close verification gaps, improve test coverage, or reduce manual effort.

• Build dashboards, reports, and data pipelines that give engineering and leadership visibility into yield, test results, or other operational or test metrics.
Identfy and bridge gaps that can emerge from speedy development cycles- documentation, technical debt, etc

• Perform system-level analysis and trade studies when programs need fast, informed technical input on architecture decisions, component selection, or integration strategy.

• Work directly with design engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, test, quality, and operations teams, often simultaneously, to drive resolution on problems that don't fit neatly into one team's charter.

Required Qualifications

• BS in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering

• 5+ years of engineering experience spanning at least two of the following: systems engineering, electromechanical hardware, embedded electronics, test/integration, software or scripting, manufacturing engineering.

• Demonstrated ability to move between disparate technical domains and deliver results without extended ramp-up time.

• Hands-on experience with hardware - you've designed fixtures, debugged assemblies, run tests, or worked on a production floor, not just written requirements documents.

• Working proficiency in at least one programming/scripting language (Python, MATLAB, C++, or similar) with demonstrated application to test automation, data analysis, or tooling.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.
The Role
We are looking for Android engineers to build the native Android experience for BJAK's Android Software Engineer.

This role is for someone who cares about clean user flows, fast performance, product quality and shipping reliable mobile features used by real customers.
What You'll Own

• Build and ship Android features using Kotlin.

• Work with product and design to simplify complex user journeys.

• Integrate backend APIs and ensure mobile flows are stable, secure and reliable.

• Improve app performance, crash rate, loading states, responsiveness and memory usage.

What We're Looking For

• 3+ years of Android development experience using Kotlin.

• Strong Android fundamentals and experience shipping production apps.

• Good knowledge of Jetpack, Coroutines, Flow and modern Android architecture.

• Strong sense of mobile UX, usability, edge cases and user flows.

• Experience integrating REST APIs and debugging production issues.

• Fast execution, high ownership and strong attention to product quality.

Tech Stack

• Kotlin

• Jetpack Compose

• Android SDK

• Coroutines & Flow

• SQL / NoSQL

• TensorFlow Lite (on-device inference)

The Kind of Builder We Want

• Thinks in user journeys, not just screens.

• Moves fast without creating messy code.

• Notices UX, performance and reliability issues before users complain.

• Honest about what they personally built, what was team-owned and what impact they can or cannot claim.

This Role Is Not For

• Engineers who only want fully defined tickets.

• Developers who build screens without caring about user experience.

• People who ignore crashes, edge cases, loading states or performance.

• Engineers who move slowly in a startup environment.

Location

Launched in late 2024, IM8 grew Q1 2026 revenue nearly 6x year-over-year to $33.8M, and the company has raised full-year 2026 IM8 revenue guidance to $190M-$210M. Over 60% of revenue is generated outside the US. We are built on science, not story - our flagship Daily Ultimate Essentials carries 90 active ingredients, we run randomized controlled trials on our products, and we hold a clinical-grade standard in a category notorious for shortcuts.
Why This Role Is Different
Most editing roles are a queue: raw footage in, competent cuts out, and someone else decides whether it worked. This one isn't. At our growth rate, creative has to scale faster than the rest of the business or it becomes the bottleneck - we already generate hundreds of millions of views from AI-driven campaigns, and every video is a brand promise made in the first three seconds. On a subscription model with the LTV we're building, a hook that doesn't land isn't just a weak post - it's paid spend burned and a customer we never met. We need someone who treats the edit as a brand asset, not a service desk.
The Opportunity
We are looking for a Video Editor - IM8, to own the day-to-day creation of scroll-stopping video across every social platform: direct-response ads, organic content, and long-form brand-building films. You are a master of pacing and storytelling, fluent from high-end editorial to direct response, and comfortable taking a brief and adding your own creative spin.

• Ensure a consistent look and feel across all video content, working within brand guidelines while finding room to push creative boundaries.

What We're Looking For

• 2-5 years in video editing, with a portfolio of polished, high-quality short-form social content that demonstrates mastery of pacing, storytelling, and advanced technique.

• Video ads produced for high-growth eCommerce brands, across both editorial and direct-response styles.

• Command of advanced editing - creative transitions, visual effects, and innovative methods that elevate content beyond standard cuts.

We hire across the full data center lifecycle, from securing land and power to designing electrical and cooling systems, overseeing construction, commissioning facilities, and supporting site operations.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Recruiter to join our Data Center Infrastructure recruiting team. You’ll own searches from intake through offer and start, partnering closely with hiring managers, recruiters, and sourcers across sites and regions. Your portfolio will span specialized technical searches and recurring site-based hiring. You might open an electrical design search, build a local pipeline for construction managers, and close a commissioning lead ahead of a site handover.

In this role, you will:

- Build relationships with hiring managers before searches open to understand site milestones and anticipate hiring needs.

- Lead search intake, align on what each hire needs to deliver, and calibrate candidate profiles and interview criteria with the hiring team.

- Develop and execute sourcing strategies with sourcers and through direct outreach. Map local contractors and project owners for site-based roles and search across regions for specialized talent.

- Manage multiple searches across sites and reset priorities with hiring managers as build schedules shift. Coordinate interviewer coverage and keep candidates informed.

- Use pipeline data and candidate feedback to identify bottlenecks, test sourcing assumptions, and keep interviews and debriefs moving.

- Keep leaders informed about which hires and start dates are on track and where they need to make a decision.

- Own the candidate relationship from first outreach through start. Set clear expectations about the work and any site, travel, or relocation requirements.

- Lead closing conversations, bring in the right leaders to answer candidate questions, and coordinate offer approvals and start dates.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

- Full-cycle recruiting experience for technical or operational teams, with a track record of supporting multiple hiring managers and balancing specialist searches with recurring hiring across sites.

• Free specialized training and certification in orthopedic bracing.

Requirements
• Active physical therapist or physical therapist assistant license in the state where you practice.
• Currently working in home health or another in-home setting.
• You evaluate and provide treatment.

How to apply
Complete the short questionnaire. It asks about your license, your setting, and your caseload, and it asks you to acknowledge that teletherapy referrals begin after six fittings. A clinical onboarding specialist will reach out within one business day.

title: Talent Discovery Sourcer
description:
Some roles can’t be filled with a standard search. Talent Discovery is the part of MongoDB’s Talent Acquisition team that finds and builds relationships with the people we want to hire. As a Talent Sourcer on the Talent Discovery team, you’ll work on our hardest-to-fill, niche, and business-critical roles, and build talent pipelines for the roles we hire for again and again. This work is deep research and real conversations: you’ll dig into adjacent markets and unconventional talent pools, find people who aren’t looking, and earn their interest in MongoDB.

You’ll partner with recruiters and hiring managers to understand what a search really needs, build a targeted plan for finding it, and hand off strong, well-documented slates and pipelines as candidates move into formal interviews.

This role can be based out of our office or remotely in the United States.

In this role, you will

• Own and drive the sourcing plan. Turn hiring needs into a clear search strategy, align stakeholders on the target profile, and lead the approach from there

• Map talent markets. Use tools like Gem, SeekOut, LinkedIn Recruiter, GitHub, and X-ray search to research scarce talent pools and track talent movement, including competitors, adjacent markets, and emerging companies and geographies.

• Reach out to candidates with intent. Write personal, informed outreach that reflects each person’s background and what would motivate them, not keyword matching.

• Build long-term relationships. Engage and nurture passive candidates over time, so MongoDB is top of mind when the right role opens.

• Qualify beyond the resume. Run conversations that surface what motivates each candidate, and keep them informed and interested as searches progress.

• Hand off with full context. Present qualified slates and pipelines to recruiters and hiring managers, including each candidate’s background, motivations, fit, and history.

• Share what you learn. Bring market insight back to the recruiting team, such as where talent is and what competitors are doing.

• Keep the CRM/ATS clean. Keep search progress, pipeline health, and relationship history visible to the whole team.

You are someone who has

• 2 years of experience in sourcing, research, or recruiting, ideally including niche or hard-to-fill searches

• Sharp research instincts and the confidence to take an unclear hiring need and shape it into a clear search strategy

• A track record of engaging passive candidates and sustaining those relationships over time

• Working knowledge of sourcing and market-intelligence tools (e.g., Gem, SeekOut, LinkedIn Recruiter, GitHub, X-ray search, or equivalents)

• Experience using AI in sourcing and research, and good judgment about where it helps and where human judgment has to lead

• Excellent written and verbal communication, and the ability to build trust with someone who isn’t looking for a job

• Strong attention to data hygiene and follow-through

• A collaborative mindset: you’ll work closely with recruiters and hiring managers, and you want to see your work turn into hires
